newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INSTANT VIEW-Portugal May CPI 0.7 pct mth/mth.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Portugal May CPI 0.7 pct mth/mth.

text.p: The following are analysts' reactions to Portugal May CPI data.

"The CPI data is distinctly bad and is a surprise. It will probably prevent the Bank of Portugal from cutting rates tomorrow. I find some solace when I consider that food and drink is the main reason for the rise in prices, which indicates that the long-term drop in prices is not in jeopardy."
JORGE FERRAZ, INFORMACAO DE MERCADOS FINANCEIROS

"May inflation was far higher than expected. Faced with these numbers, the Bank of Portugal has no room to cut rates tomorrow. A rate cut next week will depend on developments in the forex market. International events will have to calm down (for a rate cut to be possible), in terms of the evolution of the mark-franc and mark-peseta."

"This CPI is not going to help the short bonds, although our spreads are so wide with Spain that it does not worry me much. It breaks the trend of excellent performance that we have had, but, in terms of the average rate, I think that by the end of the year we will not have to alter our estimates much, although we shall probably be closer to the top end of the government's forecast range (2.25-2.50 percent)."
PEDRO BRAZ TEIXEIRA, BANCO SANTANDER DE NEGOCIOS PORTUGAL:
"The rise is not very pleasant but it is essentially concentrated in two particular items. It is not a generalised rise in prices and, in principle, does not put the government's target at risk."
